name: Pendlay Row
movementPattern: Horizontal pull - parallel torso from floor
grip: Pronated (overhand) grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
description: Perform a strict bent-over barbell row starting from a dead stop on the floor for each repetition, maintaining a strictly horizontal torso parallel to the ground.
setup: Step up to a loaded barbell on the floor with feet hip-width apart.
Hinge deeply at the hips and bend knees until torso is strictly parallel to the floor.
Grip the barbell with an overhand pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Brace the core, flatten the spine, and take the slack out of the barbell.
instructions: Explosively pull the barbell upward from the floor by driving elbows toward the ceiling.
Contact the barbell against the lower chest or upper abdomen without standing up or raising torso angle.
Lower the barbell under control all the way back to a dead stop on the floor.
Reset spinal tension completely between every repetition.
cues: Torso stays parallel like a table.
commonMistakes: Rising the torso into a 45-degree angle to heave the bar upward.
Bouncing the bar off the floor instead of pulling from a complete dead stop.
Rounding the lower spine under heavy loads.

logging.example: Bar (20 kg) plus 50 kg plates: record 70 kg total barbell mass.
logging.note: Record total combined mass of the barbell and loaded plates.

variantNote: Strict dead-stop barbell row with horizontal torso parallel to the floor. Eliminates stretch-shortening cycle momentum.
